title: Replace the brief-length gate with per-agent entry invariants
context: With the brief-length gate removed, no categorical property of a brief's text says whether it re-explains context the parent already holds. A replacement was needed that an agent can prove about itself rather than a container sized to fit scenarios that cannot be enumerated in advance.
options: No replacement; accept that a wrong dispatch is undetected
A routing skill that advises before dispatch
Per-agent entry invariants asserted as the first field of the output contract, with the agent halting on failure
outcome: Each agent's first returned field is its own precondition, proven with a command and its exit code, and the agent halts rather than proceeding when the check fails. code-reviewer proves a non-empty diff exists; conformance-auditor proves both a named standard and a named artifact resolve to real paths; machinist enumerates and counts the files its brief names and halts at a count of zero, because a brief that cannot name its targets was not fully specified. A wrong dispatch is therefore discovered in the agent's first action rather than after three rework rounds. The residual risk — that a cold dispatch which should have been a fork still proceeds — is recorded as accepted in SPEC section 10.1 rather than papered over with another advisory rule.
